stamp: {"keys":[{"id":"k","problem":"The icons on the fund labels are weak and do not help tell the labels apart.","where":"the labels on fund rows","kind":"taste"}],"liked":[]}

raised: The 'מס רק במכירה' popup stayed open on every screen, covering numbers such as the yearly-return box, the % input and the hedging tables
Ylin Lapidot has only one year of history, and the page doesn't say whether its 0% fee is a launch offer that could go up
The cost breakdown bar has too many colours
The coloured tags in the fund list were confusing
The Psagot pricing note about standing orders ('3 of the 15 banks') was hard to follow
The foreign funds have no price and need forms; the reader would drop them
The year-by-year hedging table was too much (and partly hidden); the reader would drop it
The coloured four-factor line chart and the dollar-since-2002 chart were ignored; the reader would drop them
The '+0.37%' figures were unclear: plus relative to what?
'4D' and '4A' were not explained
The difference between a tracker fund and an ETF, and why ETFs cost more, was unclear
'Tax on the currency change too' was unclear: is tax owed on a gain that came only from the dollar?
'עמלות זו על זו' (fees on fees) in the colour legend was not understood
'עוד לא נאסף' (not collected yet) was unclear: collected by whom?
The page doesn't explain exactly how tax is worked out at the end (25% on profit? anything for age?)
There is no ready answer for a 5-year horizon
There is no information on how safe the money is if the broker or fund manager fails
There is no guidance on how to start (opening an account, setting up a standing order)
There is nothing to tell the top two funds apart beyond the 43 ₪ (size, age, stability)
The reader would drop the per-broker list of advert claims
The reader would drop the 'not in the calculation' discounts for young people and soldiers

problems.why: The reader says the coloured tags in the fund list confused them, but the details they give are about what the text means (4D, +0.37%), not about the icons on the labels being weak or not helping to tell the labels apart.
